title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' (c. 1981–84) part of Grothendieck's notes. He studies the Galois/Teichmüller-type automorphism group of the profinite fundamental groupoid of M_{0,3} with tangential base points and compares it with a group built from the genus-one / SL_2 level.

Objects. S_0 M_{0,3}^{!~} is a group of triples (α,β,f). Here u_{α,β} is an automorphism determined by its action on two standard generators, and f is an element of the fundamental group. The multiplication (34) on the previous page is u'' = u' u and f'' = u_{α',β'}(f) f'. This is exactly the twisted composition law familiar from the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group: (λ,f)(λ',f') = (λλ', f·F_{λ,f}(f')).

SM_{ρ,σ} is defined in (35) as a semidirect product SG*_{ρ,σ} ⋉ G. The action goes through a homomorphism Θ to (outer) automorphisms of G. G is apparently GL_2 regarded as a group scheme, so that G(Ẑ) = GL(2,Ẑ). ρ and σ seem to refer to the two elliptic elements: SL_2(Z) is generated by an element of order 6 and one of order 4. On the next page SG*_{ρ,σ} is embedded in B'_0 × T_ρ × N'_σ, i.e. a Borel-type factor, a torus and a torus normaliser.

This page.
(37) For S = Spec Ẑ the previous constructions give a group homomorphism S_0 M_{0,3}^{!~} → SM_{ρ,σ}(Ẑ)/Σ̃.
(38) Σ̃ = Σ_0 × {±1} ≅ (Z/2)^3. Σ_0 ≅ (Z/2)^2 is a subgroup of SG*_{ρ,σ} acting trivially on G, hence normal. {±1} is the centre of SL(2,Ẑ) ⊂ GL(2,Ẑ) = G(Ẑ). Taking the quotient by Σ̃ absorbs three sign ambiguities, on α, on β and on f. In effect, the genus-0 'loop equation' data determine an element of a genus-one/SL_2-type group up to these signs.
(39) He then defines G_a → S_0 M_{ρ,σ} by λ ↦ (α = ε_0(λ), β = ε_0(λ), μ = 1, ε = 1, f = ε_0(λ)). He claims it is a homomorphism onto a normal subgroup. To check this he uses the semidirect-product model (35).

The next page shows the mechanism: i(λ) = (λ, λ^{-1}) = λ·j(λ). In a semidirect product H ⋉ G where H acts through inner automorphisms via a map θ: H → G, the 'twisted diagonal' {(h, θ(h)^{-1})} is a normal subgroup centralising G. Quotienting by it passes from the automorphism action to the outer action. In short, the page sets up the comparison map between the genus-0 GT-type group and an SL_2/GL_2 'genus one' group, modulo signs and modulo inner automorphisms.
errors: The claim in (39) that the image of G_a is distinguished is asserted but only verified on the next page, via the semidirect-product model. Normality holds because B'_0 acts on G through inner automorphisms (twisted-diagonal argument), which the page does not state explicitly.
The precise meaning of 'G_a' and of ε_0 (a parametrised unipotent or one-parameter subgroup?) is not defined on this page. The formula is ambiguous without p. 499'.
The identification 'centre of SL(2,·) contained in GL(2,·) = G(Ẑ)' should read over Ẑ, not Z (handwriting).

ideas.what: Composition law (α,β,f)(α',β',f') with f'' = u_{α',β'}(f) f' on pairs (automorphism parameters, path element)
ideas.modern_name: Group law of the (profinite) Grothendieck–Teichmüller group / monoid
ideas.where_published: GT only sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), without formulas

ideas.what: Homomorphism from the genus-0 (M_{0,3}) automorphism group to a semidirect product built over GL_2/SL_2 with elliptic data ρ,σ, modulo (Z/2)^3 sign ambiguities
ideas.modern_name: GT action on the profinite completion of SL_2(Z)/B_3, i.e. the genus-one level M_{1,1} of the Teichmüller tower
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the M_{0,4}/M_{1,1} 'two-level' principle only in general terms

ideas.what: Normal subgroup given by the twisted diagonal λ ↦ (λ, θ(λ)^{-1}) in a semidirect product whose action is inner
ideas.modern_name: Standard passage from Aut to Out in a semidirect product

missed.claim: An explicit construction (with sign ambiguities exactly identified as (Z/2)^3: on α, β and f) of a homomorphism from the genus-0 GT-type group to a GL_2/SL_2 'elliptic' semidirect product. This is an early, independent version of the GT action on genus one, predating Drinfeld/Ihara/Lochak–Schneps.
missed.quote: le fait de passer au quotient par Σ̃ exprimant les trois ambiguïtés de signe, sur α, sur β et sur f
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority detail and a possibly different normalisation (via tori T_ρ, normalisers N'_σ, Borel B'_0) of the genus-one GT action. Mostly of historical interest, since the action itself is now well established.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a technical step in Grothendieck's own construction of a GT-type group and its map to the genus-one/SL_2 level. This content is now known (Drinfeld, Ihara, Lochak–Schneps), and the normal-subgroup trick is routine. Its interest is mainly historical, as an explicit pre-Drinfeld formula-level treatment.
transcription_corrections: In (39) the third component is likely μ = 1 (matching 𝒰 = (α,β,μ,ε) of the previous page), not ρ = 1.
Read 'SGl(2,Ẑ) = Sl(2,Ẑ), contenu dans Gl(2,Ẑ) = G(Ẑ)': hats over Z.
The target in (37) is SM_{ρ,σ}(Ẑ)/Σ̃ with a crossed-out fragment; the superscript on S_0 M_{ρ,σ} in (39) is struck out.
'Ga' in (39) is probably G_a (or a hatted variant); uncertain from handwriting.
